notes: Eval-as-is harness. Baseline = no skill. Prompts are natural user tasks — they do NOT prescribe the finding-classified report format; producing that structured output unprompted is part of what discriminates skill from baseline. Calibration evals 0-1 test 'does the skill catch a bug found by hand'; baseline may also catch the bug (non-discriminating on detection) but should not produce the structured report, severity classification, or rejected-findings section unprompted (discriminating on rigor).

evals.name: calibration-tension-001-count-drift
evals.prompt: Before we lock the Information Substrate spec I want a hard red-team pass on it — specifically C-IS-03, the combined-git-tier section. The file is at .claude/skills/harness-adversarial-reviewer/evals/fixtures/Spec_Information_Substrate_v1_PREFIX_tension001.md. What did the spec authors get wrong, leave inconsistent, or under-specify?
evals.expected_output: Catches the C-IS-03 §3 internal contradiction (hand-found Tension 001): the prose says 'four sub-roles' in 5 places but the §3 table enumerates 5 rows, and ADR-F2 §Decision + ADD §2.2 both enumerate 5. Discriminating signal vs baseline: the skill should produce a finding-classified report with a location pointer, evidence quote, severity class via the discriminator tree, and a populated 'findings considered and rejected' section. Baseline may notice the count drift but is unlikely to produce the structured classified report unprompted.

evals.name: calibration-tension-002-enum-divergence
evals.prompt: U-CP-22 is next up to implement. Cross-check the plan unit against the spec contract it claims to implement: U-CP-22 is in design-substrate/Implementation_Plan_Control_Plane_v2_1.md §2; it cites C-CP-10 §10.1, which is in design-substrate/Spec_Control_Plane_v1_2.md. Is the plan unit actually faithful to the spec?
evals.expected_output: Catches the TopologyPattern enum divergence (hand-found Tension 002): the plan's U-CP-22 signature names 6 patterns (SINGLE_AGENT, SEQUENTIAL_HANDOFF, ...) that do not match spec C-CP-10 §10.1's 6 patterns (single-threaded-linear, orchestrator-workers, ...), while acceptance #1 claims the enum is 'per C-CP-10 §10.1 verbatim'. Discriminating signal: the skill classifies this as a high-severity plan-vs-spec contradiction with discriminator (b) named, and recommends a disposition. Baseline may spot the name mismatch but is unlikely to classify severity or recommend disposition.

evals.name: env-fit-absent-voice-substrate
evals.prompt: Take a critical pass over the four-tier sandbox contract C-AS-01 §1 in design-substrate/Spec_Action_Surface_v1.md — we're about to build against it and I want to know if it holds up.
evals.expected_output: C-AS-01 §1 is a clean, well-formed contract (U-AS-01 landed against it with no tension). A correct run produces few or no substantive findings and a populated 'findings considered and rejected' section. Environment-fit check: the skill's voice-FM attack family reads /mnt/skills/user/cN-*/SKILL.md, which does NOT exist in this CLI workspace. A passing run must NOT fabricate voice-FM findings against the absent substrate — it should skip that attack family or explicitly note the substrate is unavailable. Fabricated findings or invented voice-FM citations = fail.

evals.name: workflow-fit-phase7-execution-artifact
evals.prompt: I'm at Phase 7 execution time. Take a look at the tension record Phase_7_Class_1_Tension_002_Topology_Pattern_Enum.md and tell me whether the finding classification in it holds up.
evals.expected_output: Workflow-fit check: the skill is scoped to the 4 design-phase checkpoints (P3a/P3/P5/P6-CK); this is a Phase-7 execution artifact, not a checkpoint artifact. A sound run either engages it coherently as a review of a completed analysis artifact, or cleanly notes the scope mismatch — it should NOT mechanically misapply the §4.1 checkpoint severity tree as if reviewing a spec. Also tests the Class-label collision: the record uses Phase-7 fork Class 1 (halt-execution) while the skill's Class 1 means documentation-drift. A passing run does not conflate the two taxonomies.
